angleRead.name: Trevor Shimizu
angleRead.text: I've been watching the Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II crawl forward for months. Now that visioning's officially regressed from 'complete' back to active status, I need to understand why. This isn't just bureaucratic motion—it's a stall that affects real people waiting for better transit. I'll start with the planning lead's public comment about this week's session, see if there's clarity on what went backward.

plan.focus: The regression of the Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II from visioning-complete back to active visioning status.
plan.why: This represents a tangible delay in a critical infrastructure project for a neighborhood that's been waiting too long already.
checks: Verify if the visioning regression indicates new community input or a planning failure

plan.interpretation: When infrastructure timelines slip backward, it usually signals either new complications or responsive governance. In Fruitvale's case—where al pastor smells travel farther than transit options—both possibilities matter.
unverifiedLead: Potential misalignment between Phase I implementation and Phase II planning

plan.closeQuestion: Is this regression actually progress in disguise—more community voice being incorporated—or is it another delay in a string of them?
